VI.description: Swap MANY subVI nodes and MANY diagram constants on one block diagram\2C in one run\2C then save the VI in place.\0A\0AWHY TRAVERSE AND NOT SubVIs[]. {LV.Diagram} SubVIs[] lists the nodes of the diagram it is asked about and does NOT descend into structures\2C so every call inside a While Loop or a Case frame was invisible to this helper - it came back under socketsNotOnDiagram while sitting plainly on the diagram\2C and the caller was left with a VI still pointing at its sockets. Measured 2026-09-16 on a VI with five subVI calls\2C three on the top-level diagram and two inside a Case frame\3A diagramSubVis listed the three and socketsNotOnDiagram named the two. Verified after the change on a generated main VI whose six calls all sit inside its event loop\2C two of them additionally inside Case frames - all six are listed and five of five entries swap in one call. Traverse for GObjects walks the whole block diagram\2C which is the only difference\3B it returns GObject references\2C so each one is cast with To More Specific Class before VI Name is read or Replace is called.\0A\0AWHY IT LOOPS INSTEAD OF TAKING ONE INDEX. Driving this from outside cost 19 tool calls for a single three-class test suite\2C alternating a list call and a replace call almost every time - measured 2026-08-29. The list call is not avoidable from outside because {LV.Diagram} SubVIs[] RE-ORDERS after every Replace and the replaced node's reference dies with it\2C so an index taken before a swap means something else after it. Inside one run the ordering problem disappears\3A the references and the names are collected ONCE\2C and each swap is then addressed BY NAME through Search 1D Array.\0A\0AWHY THE LOOPS ARE NOT NESTED. They were at first\2C with SubVIs[] re-read per swap\2C and AIXML auto-indexes a tunnel that carries a refnum array into an inner loop - `the type of the sink is 1D array of SubVI Refnum` - plus two For Loops reported as members of a cycle. Collecting first and matching second needs no nesting and no shift register at all.\0A\0AWHY A SOCKET NAME MUST BE UNIQUE. Matching is by VI Name\2C so two nodes calling the same socket are indistinguishable and the wrong subject lands in the wrong case with no error at all. The caller generates one socket per slot for exactly this reason. A name that is not found gives Search 1D Array -1\2C and Index Array then clamps to element 0 - so an unmatched name silently swaps the WRONG node. The caller checks the names against the listing before calling.\0A\0AWHY CONSTANTS COME SECOND. A dynamic dispatch input is a REQUIRED terminal\2C so a class chain needs a class value\3B AIXML cannot author a class constant\2C so the caller authors a PATH constant\2C wires it\2C and it is replaced here. Order matters\3A with the nodes swapped first the wire already has a class sink and Replace re-types it. The other way round the wire has a class source and a path sink\2C and breaks.\0A\0AWHY CONSTANTS ARE TRAVERSED TOO. They were collected from {LV.Diagram} All Objects[] of the top-level diagram\2C which does not descend into structures either\2C so a seed constant inside a Case frame or a loop was never found. A second Traverse for GObjects call collects them at any depth now. Its Class Name is ONE constant\2C Constant Class Name\2C because whether a diagram constant answers to the class name Constant is NOT MEASURED - a string constant reports StringConstant and a class constant LabVIEWClassConstant\2C so it depends on whether the traversal matches descendant classes. constants seen reports how many the traversal returned\2C so a wrong class name reads as zero rather than as a mystery.\0A\0AA LABEL THAT MATCHES MORE THAN ONE CONSTANT IS NOT REPLACED. Matching is by label\2C so two constants with one label cannot say which one is meant - the user's decision of 2026-10-11 is to refuse that label and replace the others. constant matches reports\2C per requested label and in request order\2C how many constants carried it\3B only a label with exactly one match is replaced\2C and a label with none or several is skipped with the error chain passed through untouched. The per-label count is an inner loop over the collected labels - collected ONCE before any Replace\2C so the nesting does not re-read anything.\0A\0ALists are pipe separated. A pipe is illegal in a Windows path so it cannot occur inside a value\3B a newline could not be used because the runner separates its own name/value pairs that way.\0A\0ANothing is read back after a Replace\2C on purpose\3A both its reference out and its Replace output are poison - Error 1055 on the next property read\2C and because that error travels down the wire it would also stop Save.Instrument and leave the edit unwritten. Verify by AIXML-exporting the VI and reading target=.

Every subVI node name on the diagram BEFORE the swap. Compare it with socket names - a name missing here is the silent-wrong-node case.
